name: Parkrose

boundaries.north: NE Columbia Blvd / PDX airport area

characteristics.housing_stock: 1950s-1970s ranches and split-levels, some older bungalows, manufactured homes on eastern edge
characteristics.transit_access: Moderate — MAX Blue/Red Line at Parkrose/Sumner TC, bus on Sandy and 82nd, but neighborhood is car-dependent
characteristics.crime_trend: Mixed — property crime stable, violent crime down 5% YoY
characteristics.development_pipeline: Parkrose town center planning underway, some commercial revitalization on Sandy Blvd, airport area industrial growth

investment_thesis: Lowest entry point in Portland proper. Highest distressed property concentration creates volume opportunity for rehab investors. Larger lots compared to inner neighborhoods support ADU potential. Airport proximity is a double-edged sword — noise concern but employment access. The MAX station at Parkrose/Sumner TC provides transit connectivity that many outer neighborhoods lack. Best strategy is volume: buy multiple cheap distressed properties, do solid but not luxury rehabs, and sell to first-time buyers priced out of inner Portland.
risk_factors: Airport noise on northern blocks — check flight path maps carefully
